controls.title: Expose sensitive APIs only in secure contexts
controls.mechanism: Apply WebIDL [SecureContext] to a sensitive interface or member so it is not exposed in non-secure contexts.
controls.review_question: Does every sensitive entry point use [SecureContext], or an equally explicit secure-context gate with a defined failure?
limitations: Secure contexts improve transport authentication, confidentiality, and integrity but do not provide complete application isolation.

controls.title: Use the shared potentially-trustworthy decision
controls.mechanism: Use the platform algorithm for potentially trustworthy origins and URLs instead of inventing a feature-specific transport trust test.
controls.review_question: Does the specification reuse the Secure Contexts trustworthiness algorithm and define a fail-closed result when it returns not trustworthy?
limitations: The algorithm intentionally recognizes local and user-agent-designated development contexts; review those exceptions separately.

controls.title: Specify and register a powerful feature
controls.mechanism: Give each powerful feature a lowercase name, define its descriptor and permission behavior, and register it in the Permissions Registry.
controls.review_question: Has the feature completed the Permissions integration contract, including a stable name, descriptor semantics, and registry entry?
limitations: A permission state is an input to authorization; it does not replace feature-specific checks or trusted UI.

controls.title: Deny permission in insecure or policy-disabled contexts
controls.mechanism: Return denied for non-secure contexts and for Documents not allowed to use the corresponding policy-controlled feature.
controls.review_question: Does the feature's permission-state algorithm compose with secure-context and Permissions Policy checks before consulting stored grants?
limitations: Worker applicability depends on the feature and on current Permissions Policy coverage.

controls.title: Define permission lifetime and revocation behavior
controls.mechanism: Specify a feature-appropriate permission lifetime and ensure expiry or user revocation updates dependent state and returns to the default state.
controls.review_question: Are grant lifetime, expiry, revocation, and dependent-resource cleanup explicit and proportionate to sensitivity?

evidence.section: 4 Specifying a powerful feature: permission lifetime

limitations: User agents retain latitude over permission lifetime, so specifications should not assume a persistent grant.

controls.title: Define a policy-controlled feature and default allowlist
controls.mechanism: Assign a feature token and explicit default allowlist so top-level availability and cross-origin delegation are defined without deployment policy.
controls.review_question: Is the API a policy-controlled feature with a justified default allowlist, preferably no broader than the minimum required?
limitations: The framework defines `*` and `self` defaults; choosing `self` for sensitive features is a review synthesis, not a universal normative rule.

controls.title: Bound delegation through inherited and container policy
controls.mechanism: Compute child availability from parent inherited policy plus the container policy; a child cannot widen an inherited denial.
controls.review_question: Does embedded use require explicit delegation, and can any descendant or response policy widen authority beyond its parent?
limitations: The cited draft explicitly notes unresolved Worker and Worklet coverage.

controls.title: Provide enforced and report-only policy delivery
controls.mechanism: Support response-level enforcement, per-container delegation, and report-only violation observation without confusing report-only with enforcement.
controls.review_question: Are enforcement, delegation, and reporting paths defined, and is report-only state kept non-authorizing?
limitations: Reporting can expose embedding policy and cross-origin behavior; consult the specification's privacy and security section.

controls.title: Constrain resource, connection, and execution destinations
controls.mechanism: Use CSP response policies and fetch directives to constrain where active content and network connections can load from, with explicit fallback behavior.
controls.review_question: Can deployments restrict every new fetch or execution surface using an existing CSP directive or a defined integration point?
limitations: CSP is deployment policy and defense in depth; it does not repair unsafe application logic.

controls.title: Gate inline and dynamically trusted code
controls.mechanism: Require matching nonces or hashes for inline script and model `strict-dynamic` as explicit delegation from a trusted root script.
controls.review_question: Does the execution model avoid ambient string-to-code authority and make any nonce, hash, or delegated trust boundary explicit?
limitations: Nonce reuse, nonce hijacking, and script gadgets remain material risks.

controls.title: Control embedding and document capabilities
controls.mechanism: Use `frame-ancestors` to constrain embedders and `sandbox` to remove document capabilities unless explicitly restored.
controls.review_question: Does the feature introduce embeddable privileged UI or documents that need ancestor restrictions or sandbox integration?
limitations: Embedding restrictions and feature delegation solve different problems and may both be required.

controls.title: Separate CSP observation from enforcement
controls.mechanism: Use Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only for deployment observation while retaining an independently enforced policy.
controls.review_question: Are report-only policies clearly non-enforcing, and can reports avoid leaking sensitive URLs or data?
limitations: Violation reports can contain sensitive information and are attacker-influenced telemetry.

controls.title: Type injection sinks
controls.mechanism: Identify injection sinks and require the corresponding non-spoofable Trusted Type rather than an unconstrained string.
controls.review_question: Does the API accept strings that become HTML, script, or script URLs, and if so can the sink require the correct Trusted Type?
limitations: Trusted Types targets DOM XSS injection sinks and does not eliminate script gadgets or cross-document vectors.

controls.title: Require Trusted Types and restrict policy creation
controls.mechanism: Use CSP `require-trusted-types-for` to enforce sink typing and `trusted-types` to restrict which policy names can be created.
controls.review_question: Can a deployment enforce Trusted Types for the new sink and limit policy creation to reviewed policy names?
limitations: A broadly permissive policy factory can recreate ambient authority under a typed wrapper.

controls.title: Treat the default Trusted Types policy as a bounded compatibility path
controls.mechanism: If a default policy converts legacy strings, define its validation, failure, and scope rather than relying on silent universal conversion.
controls.review_question: Is any default-policy conversion narrow, auditable, and fail-closed on rejected input?
limitations: This control is review synthesis; the specification defines the mechanism but cannot validate application-specific sanitizer quality.

controls.title: Upgrade or block mixed content before use
controls.mechanism: Upgrade eligible insecure subresource requests and block remaining mixed-content requests or responses according to the mixed-content algorithms.
controls.review_question: Can the feature fetch or embed insecure resources from a secure context, and is every request classified for upgrade or blocking before use?

evidence.section: 4.4 Should fetching request be blocked as mixed content?

limitations: Automatic upgrade does not guarantee that the target supports HTTPS; failure behavior remains observable.

controls.title: Offer declarative insecure-request upgrade and inheritance
controls.mechanism: Allow a document to declare insecure-request upgrading and propagate the policy to nested contexts as defined by the specification.
controls.review_question: Does the feature respect the client upgrade state before request dispatch, including nested contexts and WebSockets where applicable?
limitations: The cited W3C snapshot is from 2015; check current CSP, Fetch, Mixed Content, and HTML integrations before asserting present implementation behavior.

controls.title: Verify subresource bytes against strongest integrity metadata
controls.mechanism: Parse integrity metadata, select the strongest recognized algorithm present, and verify fetched bytes before use.
controls.review_question: Can remotely hosted executable or security-sensitive resources carry integrity metadata, and does verification select the strongest recognized metadata?

evidence.section: 3.3.3 Get the strongest metadata from set

limitations: Integrity metadata authenticates expected bytes, not the safety or provenance of the expected content.

controls.title: Block missing or mismatching integrity under Integrity Policy
controls.mechanism: Fail resource use on integrity mismatch and optionally require integrity metadata for covered request destinations with enforce or report-only policy.
controls.review_question: Is the failure mode blocking for integrity mismatch, and can deployments require integrity metadata for the new resource type?
limitations: Integrity Policy Level 2 remains a Working Draft and covered destinations are specification-defined.

controls.title: Expose trustworthy request context for server-side isolation
controls.mechanism: Attach user-agent-controlled Sec-Fetch-Dest, Mode, Site, and User metadata so servers can reject requests inconsistent with intended use.
controls.review_question: Can a server distinguish cross-site, navigation, subresource, and user-activated requests before performing a sensitive action?
limitations: The headers provide context, not a complete authorization decision; servers need an explicit allow policy and compatibility handling.

controls.title: Minimize referrer disclosure
controls.mechanism: Define policy delivery and strip sensitive URL components before producing a Referer value, with more restrictive policy available for capability-bearing URLs.
controls.review_question: Can API URLs contain identifiers or capabilities that would leak through referrers, and is an appropriate restrictive policy defined?

evidence.section: 8.4 Strip URL for use as a referrer

limitations: This immutable W3C snapshot predates the current Fetch living-standard default; verify current Fetch before asserting default behavior.

controls.title: Define origin-bound data clearing and execution-context invalidation
controls.mechanism: Provide targeted clearing types for cache, cookies, storage, and execution contexts and execute clearing before rendering the triggering response.
controls.review_question: Can a site reliably revoke local state and prevent still-running same-origin contexts from immediately recreating it?
limitations: The 2017 draft acknowledges incomplete clearing and remnants outside browser-controlled stores.

controls.title: Bind credential operations to origin, ancestors, and mediation
controls.mechanism: Check same-origin-with-ancestors, apply mediation requirements, and support preventSilentAccess so credential retrieval does not become ambient cross-origin authority.
controls.review_question: Are credential collection, storage, and presentation origin-bound and subject to explicit mediation where silent access is inappropriate?
limitations: Credential mediation cannot prevent all chooser, timing, or origin-confusion attacks; those are separate review surfaces.

controls.title: Bind session refresh to a scoped device key proof
controls.mechanism: Scope a device-bound session, refresh only eligible requests, and prove possession of a securely stored session key using the defined protocol.
controls.review_question: Are session scope, refresh eligibility, challenge handling, key creation, and proof verification all origin-bound and fail-closed?

evidence.section: 8.3 Identify if a request is allowed to refresh

limitations: DBSC reduces cookie-theft risk but does not stop an attacker executing in the active browser context or replace server authorization.

controls.title: Constrain cryptographic capability by context, extractability, and usage
controls.mechanism: Expose sensitive cryptographic operations only in secure contexts and represent keys as opaque capabilities with explicit extractability and permitted usages.
controls.review_question: Are key material, exportability, permitted operations, and algorithm normalization constrained to the minimum required capability?
limitations: The API exposes primitives, not protocol safety; authors must still define algorithm, parameter, lifecycle, and key-management requirements.

controls.title: Require and enforce document configuration preconditions
controls.mechanism: Let a caller require document policy values and block a response that is incompatible with the required policy.
controls.review_question: Can an embedder state minimum document behavior and reject a response that does not commit to compatible policy values?

evidence.section: 9.7 Should response be blocked due to document policy?

limitations: The charter lists Document Policy with incubation draft state; do not present this editor draft as a stable Recommendation.

controls.title: Discover password-change UI only from a trustworthy origin
controls.mechanism: Generate the fixed `.well-known/change-password` URL only for a potentially trustworthy origin and use temporary redirects to the actual UI.
controls.review_question: Is discovery bound to the account origin and secure transport, with redirect behavior constrained and handled explicitly?

evidence.source_title: A Well-Known URL for Changing Passwords

limitations: The mechanism discovers UI; it does not authenticate the user or define password-change authorization.

controls.title: Bind passkey endpoint discovery to HTTPS and RP ID
controls.mechanism: Host the passkey endpoints JSON at an HTTPS URL derived from the relying party identifier, forbid redirects, and require a successful JSON response shape.
controls.review_question: Is endpoint discovery same-RP, HTTPS-only, non-redirecting, and strict about response status and media type?

evidence.source_title: A Well-Known URL for Relying Party Passkey Endpoints
A Well-Known URL for Relying Party Passkey Endpoints

limitations: Endpoint URLs still lead to application workflows whose authentication, authorization, and anti-CSRF properties require separate review.
